text:
Ellen: quick sync after today's deploy. Two signals from pilots: one customer (Pilot-A) is asking for an SLA commitment on 99th latency for streaming; ops telemetry also shows a small regression on long sessions. simultaneously, product has ~12 small follow-on asks (docs, onboarding, a tiny flow change). do we commit to an SLA promise now or fix first then discuss SLA?

Marco: we shouldn't promise an SLA until we verify baseline. if Pilot-A needs a commercial commitment we can offer a timeboxed remediation plan + a measured SLO target, not an immediate SLA.

Priya: Pilot-A is asking for a written commitment before billing expansion. they want 99th <500ms for 10k tokens. that's tight but maybe achievable after fixes.

Dev: quick numbers: staging p99 for long sessions currently ~720ms, p95 ~310ms. error uplift negligible. root cause looks like occasional KV cache pressure during sustained multi-turns. estimate: 4 eng-days to implement KV reclaim heuristics + 1 day for canary and validation.

Ellen: tradeoff: if we spend full squad on the fix, polish backlog stalls. Pilot-A is high-cred; losing them would hurt ARR.

Marco: proposal: 3-phase approach. Phase A (48h): urgent mitigation + temporary guardrails (server-side pacing + client-side best-practice doc) to hit intermediate SLO: p99 <650ms. Phase B (next 7 days): targeted runtime fix (Dev lead) to reach p99 <500ms under perf harness. Phase C (2-week follow-on): polish and onboarding items.

Priya: acceptance criteria for Pilot-A commitment: Phase A deployed with canary and monitoring, p99 <=650ms for 6h steady; Phase B shows p99 <=500ms under 2h 20% canary. Only then we offer a dated SLA addendum.

Dev: ops can run the canary. canary reservation request: 2 GPUs for 8h. will push a server-side pacing flag and KV reclaim change as a staged deploy.

sales-bot: Escalation logged: ESC-PILOT-A-877. Notifying #sales and #legal.

Ellen: freeze policy: block non-hotfix serving runtime merges until Phase B completes. docs and small UI PRs may continue.

Marco: mitigation steps (I'll pin in #eng-runtime):
```
1. enable flag: pacing_guard=true on canary
2. deploy kv_reclaim=v1 to canary pool
3. route 5% traffic for 2h
4. run perf-job: ./perf/run_stream --tokens 10000 --qps 30 --duration 120
5. monitor p99, p95, kv_hits, memory_pressure
```

Dev: estimate Timeline: Phase A (48h) -> Phase B (7d) -> Phase C (2wk). will create tickets with owners and ETA.

Priya: comms draft for Pilot-A: "We observed a performance edge-case in long sessions. We're deploying a two-phase remediation plan: an immediate mitigation (48h) and a follow-up runtime improvement (1 week). We'll pause rollout of new variants until Phase B verification. We can discuss an SLA addendum after Phase B meets the acceptance criteria." thoughts?

Ellen: looks good. add a line about rollback and an agreed verification window. also cc support and ops on the doc.

Marco: decision: go with phased plan. Pilot-A gets a written timeline not a guaranteed SLA yet; we commit to a measurable remediation cadence and a formal SLA review after Phase B. spin up hotfix-squad: Dev lead, 2 runtime engs. polish items moved to "post-phase-C" milestone.

Dev: opening PRs now. will tag all serving changes with label:hotfix and reference this thread_ts.

sales-bot: Sales notified with draft message. Legal loop-in pending.

Priya: I'll own Pilot-A communications and update the roadmap item with acceptance criteria.

Ellen: thanks. check-in tomorrow 09:00 PT. if mitigation doesn't hit Phase A SLO within 12h of canary, we escalate and consider temporary rollback. :white_check_mark:
